why: After wenn the verb goes to the end; the wenn part is the first element, so bleibe comes next.

p: Anna is coming if she has time. (start with Anna)
why: After wenn the verb goes to the end: wenn sie Zeit hat.

p: Lena isn't coming, because she's tired. (use denn)
why: denn does not count, so the verb stays in second place: sie ist müde.

p: I'll come if I have time.
why: After wenn the verb goes at the end, and with ich it is habe.

p: If it rains, we'll stay home.
why: Only wenn sends regnet to the end and puts bleiben right after the comma.

p: I'm not going to the movies, because I have no money.
why: denn keeps ich habe in the usual order; wenn or dass would send habe to the end.

p: If I have time, I'll come. (start with wenn)
why: After wenn the verb goes to the end, and the main verb comes next: komme ich.

p: I'm staying home because I'm sick. (use denn)
why: denn does not count, so the verb stays in second place: ich bin krank.

p: Are you coming along if it rains? (to a friend)
why: In a yes/no question the verb comes first, and after wenn the verb goes to the end.
das Gift is poison. A gift is ein Geschenk.
der Chef is the boss. A chef is ein Koch.
fast means almost. Fast (quick) is schnell.
A receipt is die Quittung; das Rezept is a recipe or a prescription.
also means so; too is auch.

p: I want a coffee. (start with ich)
why: Kaffee is masculine: einen in the accusative.

p: I'm getting a present. (start with ich)
why: The ich form ends in -e: bekomme. bekommen means get, not become.

p: Tomorrow I'm getting my new cell phone. (start with morgen)
why: Verb second: morgen first, then bekomme. Handy is neuter: mein neues Handy.
German says I have hunger: Ich habe Hunger.
How you feel takes mir: Mir ist kalt.
too is auch; also means so.
Chef is masculine: mein, not meine.

p: I'm getting a new cell phone.
why: The ich form ends in -e: bekomme.
German says have thirst, and the ich form is habe.
